summary: AI-tools rate-limit + wallet auto-debit (iteration 6) — 17/17 backend pytest cases pass and the 3 critical UI flows (BreachChecker usage bar, LimitReachedDialog with limit-signin anonymous CTA, FloatingStack FAQ 429-as-bot-bubble) verified on the live preview URL. Anonymous 429 carries auth_required=true; logged-in low-balance 429 carries top_up_required=true with correct {balance, needed, wallet_cost}; logged-in wallet path returns 200 with quota.source='wallet', cost matching tool config (10/15/49/3), debits balance, inserts a wallet_transactions debit doc with reason='AI tool · <tool>'. Per-IP isolation for anonymous, per-user isolation for logged-in (shared across IPs), and yesterday's tools_usage rows are ignored. Rule-based tools (recovery-odds, account-worth, selfie-coach) confirmed unmetered. Admin bypass via X-Admin-Token+ADMIN_TOKEN env works.

minor.issue: When XposedOrNot returns 404 (clean email) the endpoint returns 200 BUT does NOT include `quota` in the response body (early-return path at line 2666 in server.py). Frontend currently coerces missing quota from /tools/usage via refreshUsage(), so it's not visible in UX — but for API consumers that rely on response.quota, the 404-path is inconsistent with the other tools. Fix: attach `quota` to the clean-result branch the same way the breached-result branch does at line 2702.

action_items: OPTIONAL: attach `quota` dict to the 404 (clean-email) early-return branch of /api/tools/breach (server.py line ~2666) to keep response shape consistent across the breach endpoint.
critical_code_review_comments: Race condition in _tools_consume_quota: the check (find_one count) and the increment (update_one $inc) are NOT atomic — two concurrent requests at count=4 can both pass the `used < daily_free` check and both decrement, leading to count=6 with 2 free uses consumed. For higher-concurrency or burst traffic, use a findOneAndUpdate with a filter expression like {count: {$lt: daily_free}} for atomic check-and-increment. Same concern for the wallet path (balance read, then $inc -cost) — could allow a user with balance=10 to make two simultaneous breach calls and go to balance=-10.

Admin bypass is keyed on the ADMIN_TOKEN env var only. The /api/admin/login endpoint mints uuid4 tokens stored in db.admin.tokens — but those CANNOT bypass the rate-limit (no DB-token check in _tools_consume_quota). Either document this clearly or also accept the per-session admin tokens.
server.py is now 4091 lines — strongly recommend splitting (tools.py, telegram.py, admin.py, auth.py). Maintainability risk is growing.
404 branch of /tools/breach returns early without `quota` in the response (see backend_issues.minor). Inconsistent with other branches.

FAQ chat history is appended to db.chat_history BEFORE the LLM call; a 429 short-circuits before either insert, which is fine — but on LLM 502, the user message was already inserted with no bot reply. Consider transactional bookkeeping.

Browser tests use the real preview-pod IP and consume the actual day's quota — note the browser-side FAQ quota was burned during testing for the floating-chat 429 test (15 calls).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Reusable pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_tools_rate_limit.py — 17 tests, ~15s wall. Pattern: import server in-process with a pre-installed asyncio loop (same trick as test_tg_bot_upgrade.py); for HTTP-level rate-limit checks against the public preview URL just seed db.tools_usage with the target {ip|user_id, tool, date} + count and send 1 request. For wallet auto-debit + admin-bypass paths the test spins up an in-process httpx ASGITransport against server.app and monkey-patches httpx.AsyncClient (for XposedOrNot) or emergentintegrations.llm.chat.LlmChat (for appeal/faq). IMPORTANT: when patching httpx.AsyncClient, save a reference to the real class BEFORE the patch so you can use it for your ASGI test client — otherwise your test client itself becomes the fake. Browser tests: floating FAQ chat panel is at data-testid='floating-faq-chat-{panel,toggle,input,send,body,close}', BreachChecker at data-testid='breach-{email-input,submit,result}', usage bar at 'usage-bar', limit dialog at 'limit-reached-dialog' with branches 'limit-signin' | 'limit-register' | 'limit-topup' | 'limit-wait'.
